context.description: The heartbeat, the wall clock and the stale cadence run independently

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of verify-spec-SV5.spec.ts (committed, sha256 prefix 873bdfd4cb189dc1); my own bun run at HEAD f57285510d: 4 pass, 0 fail, 40 expect(). The real RunSupervisor machine runs as a root actor on the xstate-effect SimulatedClock, with the real touch, stale-check and record workers, a real Recorder whose writer calls the real TaskStatus.write (wrapped only to count), and the real event store. Given a live run whose stale check is held on the checkout lock: another fiber holds the run's checkout lock; after the 1 s cadence the staleCadence region is 'checking'; the run actor is active, and only run.started is stored. When the clock advances by 5 seconds: clock.increment(5000). Then the status file is touched once with a newer heartbeat: exactly one more write after a settle wait, of the same projected status, with a larger aliveAt, and status.json on disk holds that aliveAt; the stale check still waits and no fact is recorded. The follow-up (+3 s nothing, +2 s one touch) shows the heartbeat keeps its own 5 s cadence while the check is stuck. And a touch that fails is logged and records no fact - two ways: (a) the real path - status.json is made a directory, the real write fails, TaskStatus.write logs 'the status write failed', no fact is stored, the heartbeat beats again, and the next touch writes the file; (b) a failing touch worker given through machine.provide makes the supervisor's own onError path run 3 times: 3 'a heartbeat touch failed' logs, no fact, the run stays active, no failure rule fires. I read recorder.ts: the real touch is Queue.offer(...).asVoid and cannot fail, so (b) needs the stand-in. The stand-in replaces only the worker, not the supervisor under test, and (a) covers the real failure end to end. So the stand-in hides nothing. And the run wall clock records run.ended in state failed when it expires: with runWallClock 30 min, 1 s short nothing is stored and the stale check still waits; at expiry the store holds exactly run.started then run.ended {state failed, reason 'wall clock: the run took over 30 min'}; the run actor folds to failed and done, the supervisor closes, status.json says failed, the lease release runs once. Settle sleeps come only before 'nothing more' checks; positive waits use eventually, which dies after 20 s. No gap found.
